job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his grandfather sat on their terrace in a small village near Jaipur, looking up at the clear night sky. Rohan pointed to a bright object and asked if it was a shooting star. Grandfather smiled and explained that what he saw was actually a meteor, a small piece of rock that burns up upon entering our atmosphere, not a star falling from the sky. Rohan then noticed the Moon, which appeared as a thin crescent. He wondered if clouds were hiding the rest of it. Grandfather clarified that the Moon’s phases occur because we only see the portion of the Moon illuminated by the Sun from our perspective on Earth, not because of shadows or clouds. As they looked further, Rohan noticed a bright, steady light that did not twinkle. Grandfather explained that this was a planet, which reflects sunlight, unlike stars which are massive, self-luminous bodies like our own Sun. He pointed out that the Sun is actually a typical star, just much closer to us than the distant stars we see at night. Finally, they watched the constellations slowly shift position. Grandfather explained that this apparent motion happens because the Earth rotates on its axis, not because the stars themselves are traveling across the sky.

items.evidence: Grandfather explained that what he saw was actually a meteor, a small piece of rock that burns up upon entering our atmosphere, not a star falling from the sky.
items.q: A bright streak flashes across the night sky and vanishes. What is it most likely?
options: A rock fragment burning in the air
A star dropping out of the sky
A planet slipping out of its path
A cloud lit up by moonlight
items.explain: A meteor is a small rock that burns up in our atmosphere. It is not a falling star.

wrong.why: thinks shooting stars are real stars falling
thinks planets can leave their orbits and fall
blames clouds for what is seen in the sky

items.evidence: Grandfather clarified that the Moon’s phases occur because we only see the portion of the Moon illuminated by the Sun from our perspective on Earth, not because of shadows or clouds.
items.q: Why does the Moon sometimes look like a thin crescent?
options: We see only a small lit part of it
Earth's shadow covers most of its face
Clouds hide the rest of its surface
It shrinks and grows over each month
items.explain: We see only the part of the Moon lit by the Sun, so it can look thin.

wrong.why: thinks Earth's shadow causes the phases
thinks clouds hide parts of the Moon
thinks the Moon itself changes size

items.evidence: Grandfather explained that this was a planet, which reflects sunlight, unlike stars which are massive, self-luminous bodies like our own Sun.
items.q: Rohan sees a bright light that shines steadily without twinkling. What does this suggest?
options: It is a planet shining by borrowed light
It is a star giving out its own light
It is a planet that makes its own light
It is a star that is very close by
items.explain: A steady light is a planet, which only reflects sunlight. Stars make their own light.

wrong.why: thinks all bright steady lights are stars like twinkling ones
thinks the nearest light must be a star

items.evidence: He pointed out that the Sun is actually a typical star, just much closer to us than the distant stars we see at night.
items.q: The Sun looks far bigger and brighter than night stars. How is it still a star?
options: It is a typical star that is much nearer
It is a unique body unlike any star
It is a planet that burns very brightly
It is a larger star than all others
items.explain: The Sun is a typical star. It looks different only because it is much closer to us.

wrong.why: thinks the Sun is not a star because it looks different
thinks the Sun differs from stars in kind, not distance
thinks looking bigger means it really is bigger

items.evidence: Grandfather explained that this apparent motion happens because the Earth rotates on its axis, not because the stars themselves are traveling across the sky.
items.q: Why do the constellations seem to shift position during the night?
options: The Earth turns on its axis
The stars travel from East to West
The Earth moves in a perfect circle
The Moon pulls the stars along
items.explain: The Earth rotates on its axis, so the stars only appear to move across the sky.

wrong.why: thinks stars really move across the sky
confuses rotation with orbiting in circles
invents the Moon as the cause
